findings.title: Team admin/owner check requires being both admin and owner
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...). Team membership roles are distinct, so a user who is only a team admin or only a team owner fails this check. Non-organizer team admins/owners who should be able to manage a team booking are therefore incorrectly rejected with FORBIDDEN unless they also happen to be the organizer or an attendee. The condition should be an OR.

findings.title: Any attendee can add arbitrary guests without organizer approval
findings.body: The handler authorizes the request if the caller is merely listed as an attendee (isAttendee based on matching email). The UI only exposes Add Guests to the booking owner in their bookings list, but the API allows any attendee with a Cal.com account using the same email to add arbitrary people to someone else's booking, triggering calendar updates and invitation emails to all attendees. This exceeds the organizer-only capability exposed by the product UI.

findings.title: Duplicate and case-variant guests are not deduplicated server-side
findings.body: uniqueGuests only filters out emails exactly equal to an existing attendee and does not deduplicate within the submitted guests array itself, and all comparisons are case-sensitive while the blacklist check lowercases only the blacklist entries (guest is not lowercased). The server schema in addGuests.schema.ts likewise has no uniqueness refinement. A direct API call with ['a@x.com','a@x.com'] or case variants such as 'A@x.com' vs existing 'a@x.com' creates duplicate Attendee rows, duplicate calendar attendees and duplicate emails, and a blacklisted address can be bypassed by changing its case.

findings.title: Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending or past bookings
findings.body: The handler loads the booking by id but never checks booking.status or booking.endTime before creating attendees, calling EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees and sending 'guests added'/scheduled emails. Guests can therefore be added to cancelled or rejected bookings (reviving calendar invites for an event that will not happen) or to bookings already in the past. The server should reject non-ACCEPTED and/or past bookings regardless of what the client UI shows.

findings.title: Calendar is updated with the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's
findings.body: getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and the EventManager construction use the requesting user, not booking.user (the organizer whose calendar holds the event). When a team admin or an attendee adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees runs with the wrong user's calendar/video credentials, so it will fail to update the organizer's calendar event or attempt updates against the caller's own integrations, leaving the database attendees and the external calendar out of sync. Credentials/EventManager should be built for the booking organizer.

findings.title: Email classification uses unfiltered guests list instead of uniqueGuests
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw input `guests` rather than `uniqueGuests`. Addresses that were filtered out because they are already attendees are therefore classified inside sendAddGuestsEmails as newly added guests and receive an AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the guests-added notification, and the new/existing attendee classification no longer matches who was actually created in the database. Pass uniqueGuests.

findings.title: Unbounded guests array allows mass attendee creation and email spam
findings.body: guests is z.array(z.string().email()) with no .min(1)/.max() bound. Any authorized caller can submit thousands of addresses in one request, causing a createMany of attendee rows, an EventManager calendar update with thousands of attendees, and sendAddGuestsEmails to fan out organizer, team and per-attendee emails (plus a scheduled email to every new guest). This is an email-spam/resource-exhaustion vector; bound the array size (and reject empty arrays) server-side.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type disabled-email settings
findings.body: Unlike sendLocationChangeEmails/sendScheduledEmails, sendAddGuestsEmails does not accept eventTypeMetadata and never checks eventTypeDisableHostEmail/eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail. Event types that have standard host or attendee emails disabled (metadata.disableStandardEmails) will still send organizer, team-member and attendee emails when guests are added, violating the organizer's configured email preferences.

findings.title: MultiEmail imports @calcom/ui from inside the @calcom/ui package
findings.body: MultiEmail.tsx lives in packages/ui but imports { Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip } from '@calcom/ui' (the package's own public entrypoint, which re-exports MultiEmailLazy -> MultiEmail). This self-referential/circular import through the package index can cause circular-dependency initialization problems and pulls the entire UI index into the lazily loaded chunk, defeating the lazy loading introduced in MultiEmailLazy. Sibling form components should be imported via their relative paths inside the package.
